original.target_description: Comparison of number of violent charges for ASPD+PSY diagnosis versus controls. Primary criminal-conduct group comparison, not the supplementary severe-ASPD-only analysis or emotional-processing subsample.

n.sample_role: Analytic participants: incarcerated European American men in the two mutually exclusive final diagnostic groups (ASPD + PSY and controls); criminal-conduct analyses.
n.exclusions: ASPD + PSY: 3 univariate outliers excluded; controls: 7 univariate and 1 multivariate outlier excluded. Source-wide criminal-conduct exclusions: 3 ASPD + PSY, 4 ASPD-only, and 7 control univariate outliers plus 1 ASPD-only and 1 control multivariate outlier.
n.location: p. 801, Results: Overview of Analyses; Table 1 note
n.quote: Sample sizes were 178, 212, and 66 for control, ASPD-only, and ASPD ⫹ PSY groups in criminal ... conduct analyses; ... 3 ASPD ⫹ PSY, 4 ASPD-only, and 7 control inmates ... were identified as univariate outliers, and 1 ASPD-only inmate and ... 1 control inmate were identified as multivariate outliers; their ... exclusion left 66 ASPD ⫹ PSY inmates, 212 ASPD-only inmates, ... and 178 control inmates for analyses.

notes: Only assigned unfinished fields are populated; all other fields are placeholders. 66 + 178 = 244 participants in mutually exclusive final diagnostic groups (ASPD + PSY and controls). Group counts are explicitly final analytic counts (Table 1 and Overview of Analyses), not recruitment totals or values inferred from test degrees of freedom. The same final criminal-conduct groups apply to versatility, violent-charge and nonviolent-charge comparisons. The separately labeled severe-ASPD-only reanalysis on p. 802 changes the diagnostic definition and is not the described target.
